author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory and its JSON document to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian surfaces, the paged directory page and the reinstated JSON document, accept an optional specialty named in the address. They list only veterinarians holding it, matched on the whole name ignoring case. A blank value is ignored, and without a specialty both behave as today.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-004] given the clinic's veterinarians, when the JSON document is requested without a specialty, then it holds every veterinarian with their specialties.
[REQ-VET-003] given a specialty name, when the directory page is requested with it, then only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed, a page at a time.
[REQ-VET-003] given a specialty name, when the JSON document is requested with it, then it holds only veterinarians holding that specialty.
[REQ-VET-003] given a specialty name differing from the stored name only by letter case, when either surface is requested with it, then it matches.
[REQ-VET-003] given only the start of a specialty name, when either surface is requested with it, then no veterinarian matches.

[REQ-VET-003] given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is requested with it, then the page or document is returned as usual (HTTP 200), listing no veterinarians, and not as an error.
[REQ-VET-003] given an empty or whitespace-only specialty, when either surface is requested with it, then the result is the same as a request naming no specialty.
[REQ-VET-003] given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when the reader follows a link to another page, then that page is narrowed to the same specialty.
[REQ-VET-001] given no specialty, when the directory page is opened, then it behaves as today: every veterinarian, a page at a time.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search (NG-9, narrowed but still declined).
Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface; the filter is a URL contract only. A visible control may come as a follow-up request.
Paging the JSON document; without the parameter it behaves as today, and the request does not ask for paging.
Narrowing by any attribute other than specialty.
Trimming surrounding spaces from a non-blank specialty, or defining behavior for several specialties in one request: both recorded as PRD Open Questions, left unspecified.
notes: Owner decisions quoted in intake line 1. ID allocation (my reversible call): REQ-VET-004 is the fresh requirement the owner asked for, reinstating the JSON document at /vets as a supported surface; REQ-VET-003 is the specialty filter across both surfaces. This slice carries REQ-VET-004's baseline bullet because the filter is its first requested capability. REQ-VET-002 stays in Superseded, now pointing at REQ-VET-004. NG-9 narrowing recorded in the Non-Goals row plus non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-30-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md. For design: system-design.md still describes the JSON route as serving no requirement and pending removal (Known deviations row, Vets/VetController rows); those need updating. The ADR README index row for the new non-goal ADR is outside my write scope. Existing tests showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList may be renamed or absorbed; note which test carries each merged name. The page-size constant and the case-insensitive match under PostgreSQL (see REQ-OWN-002 edge case 3) are design questions.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Stays inside the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure). It follows the owner-search seam: an optional request parameter, a derived repository query, and a paged model (OwnerController.processFindForm and OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith, located by grep because the IDE oracle is not connected). New ground is recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-30-specialty-narrowing-as-portable-uncached-query.md: the whole-name case-insensitive match is expressed in the query (Spring Data IgnoreCase), not through vendor collation, so the REQ-OWN-002 PostgreSQL defect does not repeat, and narrowed reads bypass the unbounded vets cache. The JSON /vets route becomes a supported surface for REQ-VET-004; the 'serves no requirement' Known Defects row is removed. Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController, and CacheConfiguration now cite REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004. The Scale and Load section was added with the vet rows.
integration_points: Binding (GET /vets.html, GET /vets): the target is a request-scoped optional String 'specialty' (@RequestParam, required=false). No persisted type is bound. The controller maps a null or blank value to 'absent' (architecture-principles Web controller row: normalization is binding) and passes any other value unchanged, with no trimming (PRD Open Question, narrowest reading).

Repository: add derived narrowed reads to VetRepository, a Page variant for the directory and a Collection variant for the JSON document, e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase. Leave both uncached (no @Cacheable), @Transactional(readOnly = true). The unfiltered findAll methods and their cache stay as they are.

Template: pagination links carry the specialty only when present. Build them with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, or conditional on a non-null model attribute), never string concatenation, so the value is URL-encoded. Add no form or page control.
JSON: an empty narrowed result still returns 200 with the Vets wrapper holding an empty list.

Double, repository boundary (matching semantics: case, whole name vs prefix, several specialties, a vet with none, an unknown name, paging of the narrowed list): use the real H2-backed repository. Choose either @DataJpaTest in ClinicServiceTests (paging with a page size of 1 over 'surgery', which two seed vets hold) or a full-context MockMvc test (VetControllerIntegrationTests, following CrashControllerIntegrationTests) over the seed data. A mock stub cannot prove matching.

Double, framework transport: MockMvc (the sanctioned mock). Controller tests for binding (blank treated as absent, value passed through, 200 on empty, pagination links carrying specialty, a narrowed page model reporting totalPages > 1) may keep the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub, tolerated under testing-principles § Mocking Policy. Do not introduce a new mock framework usage elsewhere.

Test naming: the prd-entry lists every name under VetControllerTests. A matching-semantics name that needs the real repository may live in the integration class. Record in the build notes which class carries each name, and which of showVetListHtml/showResourcesVetList were renamed or absorbed.

risks.risk: Narrowed directory and JSON paths scale with the number of veterinarians (system-design § Scale and Load, narrowed row)
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: a database-side derived query, paged for the page and a whole list for the document. The size is unrecorded and treated as bounded.

risks.risk: Caching the narrowed read would key the unbounded vets cache on caller-chosen text (system-design § Threat Model, cache-growth row; security-principles § Realization, widening the exposed surface)
A vendor-dependent case match, like the REQ-OWN-002 PostgreSQL defect, that the H2 suite cannot observe (system-design § Persistence)
risks.mitigation: Use IgnoreCase in the derived query. Do not change a schema script, collation, or column type.

risks.risk: A fetch-join or filtered-collection query would truncate a narrowed vet's specialties, or list a vet twice
risks.mitigation: The filter only selects vets; specialties still load through the EAGER mapping. Use a Distinct derived query. Edge case 2 test: vet 3 (surgery and dentistry) filtered by surgery shows both specialties.

risks.risk: The specialty value reaches the query and the rendered links (security-principles § Realization: injection into data access, cross-site scripting)
risks.mitigation: Pass it only as a derived-query parameter. Build links with link-expression parameters so the value is URL-encoded, and keep default escaping on.

findings.description: The conditional link expression `${specialty != null} ? @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=...)}` is repeated verbatim across five sibling pagination links (page numbers, first, previous, next, last). The Control Flow checklist treats a conditional repeated across sibling template elements as duplication, and a future change to the narrowing parameter would have to touch five places.
findings.fix: Compute the narrowing once, for example with `th:with` on the pagination container or a small Thymeleaf fragment that takes the page number, and reference it from each link. The null-parameter rendering (`specialty=`) the implementer avoided must stay avoided.

recommendations: VetController.showResourcesVetList inlines a ternary with `addAll` spanning three lines, while the page path reads through the `findPaginated` helper with an early return. A parallel private helper such as `findVets(String specialty)` would make the two surfaces read alike. This is polish, not a defect.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: SQL injection: the request-supplied specialty reaches the database only through Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java: `Page<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName, Pageable pageable)` and the Collection overload), which bind it as a parameter. The diff adds no query text built from strings.

Template injection / XSS: the specialty goes into pagination links only as a link-expression parameter (vetList.html:30 `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), so Thymeleaf URL-encodes it and attribute-escapes it. It never enters `__${...}__` preprocessing. The change also removes the vet-list preprocessing that used to build these links (the old `@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}`). `grep -F 'specialty' src/main/resources/templates/` finds no other place where the request value is rendered. The line-20 hit is the loop variable over persisted `vet.specialties`, rendered with escaped `th:text`.

Cache exhaustion: the narrowed reads have no @Cacheable, so specialty names chosen by the caller never become keys in the `vets` cache. Only the existing unfiltered findAll methods keep @Cacheable. This matches the new threat-model row in docs/system-design.md:191.

Input handling at the boundary: the specialty is an optional String @RequestParam, and blank values become null (VetController `specialtyOrNull`), so a blank request falls back to the unfiltered path as REQ-VET-003 requires. Nothing is bound to a persisted type, so mass assignment does not apply. The value is not logged. An unknown name returns an empty result, not an error, so no exception text reaches the error page.
Exposed surface: no new route. The two existing vet GET routes gain one read-only optional parameter. No mutation, and no change to actuator exposure.

Supply chain: `git status --short build.gradle pom.xml` is empty, so no dependency changed. `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind 3.1.5 and hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final. No NVD match ran: no dependencyCheck task is configured (`./gradlew tasks --all` lists none) and this review has no network access.
Secrets sweep: the production diff (VetController.java, VetRepository.java, vetList.html) adds no credential, token or key.
